description: Compute project metrics from the CPG: cyclo, LOC, functions, classes, dead code, coupling, smells, lint

file.description: Filter metrics to a specific file path or directory. If omitted, scans entire project.

thresholds.description: Custom quality gate thresholds: {max_cyclo, max_dead_code, max_loc_per_file}

gates.description: Quality gate results with name, actual, threshold, passed

query_instructions:
Returns a JSON with metrics, quality gates, findings, and prioritized recommendations.

Use the recommendations to decide what actions to take.

general_questions_before_action: Is this finding a false positive? Verify with CPG query before acting.
What is the impact of this change? Could it break other parts?
Does this code exist because an implementation was never finished, or because it was intentionally left?
Is there a duplicate of this code elsewhere? If so, which one is the source of truth?
What is the risk of NOT making this change?

dead_code.description: Functions with no incoming CALLS edges. May be dead code or dynamically dispatched.
questions_before_removing: Is this function defined in MULTIPLE files? (duplicates vs single source)
Is the file containing this function imported by any other module? Check IMPORTS edges.
Is this a public function (no _ prefix)? It may be API even if currently unused.
Is this function part of a REGISTER pattern (registry.register, engine.register, etc.)?
Could this be an UNFINISHED implementation? Check if the file has recent git activity or TODO comments.
If this is a private function (_ prefix) in a file that IS used by others, is it an internal helper that should be kept?
Does removing this function break any imports in other files?

classification_guide.safe_to_remove: Private function, no callers, file not imported by others, no register pattern match.
classification_guide.needs_review: Public function, no callers but may be API. Ask user: integrate or delete?
classification_guide.false_positive: Has register pattern match, or is imported by other modules, or is a known entry point.

high_complexity.description: Functions with cyclomatic complexity above threshold. Indicates difficult-to-maintain code.
questions_before_refactoring: How many lines does this function have? Functions >100 lines should be split.
Is this a CLI command or entry point? These often have argument parsing mixed with logic.
Does this function mix multiple responsibilities? (parsing + validation + business logic + I/O)
Are there repeated patterns (if-elif chains, switch cases) that could be replaced with dispatch tables?
Are there deeply nested conditionals that could use guard clauses?
Is there a single block that accounts for most of the complexity? Extract it first.
What functions does it call? Could any of those be the extracted logic?
refactoring_strategies: Extract argument parsing into a separate function
Extract each conditional branch into a named helper function
Replace if-elif chains with dict dispatch or strategy pattern
Use guard clauses to reduce nesting depth
Split function by responsibility: parse → validate → execute → format output
Extract file I/O operations into dedicated functions
Move business rules into data structures instead of conditional logic

smells.description: Code smells detected by qlty: function-complexity, nested-control-flow, return-statements, etc.
questions_before_fixing: Is this smell in a high-priority file (one with many other issues)? Fix those first.
Does this smell indicate a real bug risk or just style preference?
Can this be auto-fixed? Prefer automated fixes over manual changes.
Is this smell a symptom of a deeper design issue?

lint.description: Linter issues from qlty check (ruff, bandit, eslint, etc.)
questions_before_disabling: Is this lint rule too strict for this project? Consider adjusting config, not disabling inline.
Does this lint issue mask a potential bug? Security-related issues should never be disabled.
